blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, the choice of logistics model is not about operational convenience — it is about the kind of company you are trying to be. A B2B model supports patient industrial customers and long contracts; a B2C model supports consumers who change their mind in twelve seconds; an e-commerce model supports a promise of next-day, next-hour, or instantaneous delivery. Each model requires a different warehouse, a different workforce, a different technology stack, and a different relationship with failure.

Companies that try to run all three under one roof usually deliver all three at mediocrity. Companies that choose consciously — we will be excellent at one of these and adequate at the others — tend to dominate their chosen model while competitors spread themselves thin.

If I had to name the single most common logistics mistake I have seen at board level, it would be the unwillingness to admit that being great at everything is not a strategy. It is a press release. Strategy, at this level, is the willingness to be deliberately average at what does not matter — and disproportionately excellent at what does.

items.q: According to the text, at executive level the choice of logistics model is really about…
options: the kind of company you are trying to be
items.why: "it is not about operational convenience — it is about the kind of company you are trying to be."

items.q: How does the text characterise the B2C consumer?
options: Someone who changes their mind in twelve seconds
A customer who tolerates slow delivery
A patient industrial buyer on long contracts
items.why: "a B2C model supports consumers who change their mind in twelve seconds."

items.q: According to the text, what happens to companies that run all three models under one roof?
options: They cut costs across the board
They deliver all three at mediocrity
items.why: "Companies that try to run all three under one roof usually deliver all three at mediocrity."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A company should aim to be great at every logistics model at once
Being deliberately average at some things can be strategic
Each model demands a different workforce and technology stack
Choosing one model consciously builds an advantage
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro argumenta que 'ser ótimo em tudo' não é estratégia, é press release.

items.q: The phrase "It is a press release" suggests that being great at everything is…
options: an image or claim rather than a real strategy
items.why: Inferência: 'press release' contrapõe-se a 'strategy' — soa bem, mas é discurso, não escolha real.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James defendendo sua tese diante do conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Let me put the recommendation on the table before we debate it. We run three logistics models, and we run all three at roughly the same level — which is to say, mediocre. My proposal is that we drop the third one, the e-commerce express line, and pour that capacity into the two models we actually built this company around.

I know how this sounds. Nobody likes standing in front of a board and arguing for doing less. But look at the numbers with me. The express operation has consumed a disproportionate share of our warehouse investment and our best engineers, and it still trails the market on delivery time. Meanwhile our B2B contracts — the patient, high-margin business we understand better than anyone — have been quietly starved of attention.

If we free up that workforce and that technology budget, and we redirect it, I am confident we can dominate the two models we care about within eighteen months. If we keep spreading ourselves across all three, we will stay adequate everywhere and excellent nowhere. So the question I am asking you today is not whether we can afford to cut. It is whether we can afford not to.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is James's central proposal to the board?
options: Drop the third model and redirect its capacity to the other two
Add a fourth logistics model to compete harder
Merge all three models under one warehouse
items.why: "drop the third one, the e-commerce express line, and pour that capacity into the two models…"

items.q: What does James say the express operation has done, despite heavy investment?
options: It still trails the market on delivery time
It has led the market on delivery time
It has become the highest-margin business
It has freed up engineers for other lines
items.why: "it still trails the market on delivery time" — consumiu recursos e mesmo assim fica atrás.

items.q: Which business does James say has been "quietly starved of attention"?
items.why: "our B2B contracts — the patient, high-margin business… have been quietly starved of attention."

items.q: When James closes with "whether we can afford not to," he implies that…
options: the express line will recover on its own
the board should postpone any decision
cutting the third model is optional and low-priority
not cutting carries a greater cost than cutting does
items.why: Inferência: ele inverte a pergunta — o risco real está em NÃO cortar.

items.q: How would you best describe James's stance in the speech?
options: Purely defensive of the current setup
Persuasive and willing to argue for doing less
items.why: Inferência: 'Nobody likes… arguing for doing less' — ele reconhece o desconforto mas defende o corte com dados.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We chose the model for strategic reasons, not for operational convenience." Operational convenience means…
options: the most profitable option long term
what is easiest to run day to day
items.why: Operational convenience = conveniência operacional: o que é mais fácil/cômodo de operar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Trying to lead every segment at once left us spread ___, excellent nowhere."
items.why: Spread thin = diluído: recursos espalhados demais para render em cada frente.

items.q: "A B2B technology stack cannot simply be repurposed for consumer delivery." A technology stack is…
options: the set of technologies a system is built on
items.why: Technology stack = pilha de tecnologia: o conjunto de tecnologias sobre o qual o sistema é construído.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A ___ shaped for slow industrial orders cannot easily switch to next-hour delivery."
items.why: Workforce = força de trabalho: as pessoas moldadas para um modelo não migram facilmente para outro.

items.q: "Being great at everything is not a strategy — it is a press release." Here, press release means…
options: a flattering claim with no substance behind it
items.why: No contexto, press release = comunicado: soa bem, mas é imagem, não escolha estratégica de verdade.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de decisão logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the plan to cut the express line." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will double down on the two models we understand best." To double down on means to…
options: commit more resources and effort to
items.why: Double down on = reforçar a aposta, concentrar mais recursos e foco em algo.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on dropping the express line." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Redirecting the workforce will only move the needle if we follow through." To move the needle means to…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "We keep launching models but never follow through on any of them." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
